## 12. GitHub toolbox and escalation gates

### 12.1 Audited candidates

Repository license labels refer to inspected source, not every model, dataset, service, or dependency. Repository activity is not a security or reliability certification. Exact snapshot commits appear in §21.2; recheck release notes before any future installation.

| Candidate | Actual role and platform fit | Cost/maintenance boundary | Decision |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cindy — makecindy/cindy; Apache-2.0 [G01] | Separate Electron desktop + Expo/React Native mobile companion/agent client; model/harness orchestration and recent voice features. Android is a controller of an execution desktop. | Backend not included. Free client; chosen managed service, supported plans, APIs, local inference, and voice can have costs. Broad computer/app access. | First optional trial if phone-to-PC work plus companion voice is the unmet need. No documented supported bridge into ordinary native ChatGPT persona/account memory was established. |
| SillyTavern — AGPL-3.0 [G02] | Character-focused local web interface, cards, lore, speech input/output, per-character TTS mapping. Windows host with Android browser is the conservative fit; a Termux route is documented but not officially supported/guaranteed in the FAQ. | Requires model backend and possibly voice backend; local inference and hosted services differ. Host availability/security remain work. | Best candidate to investigate for explicit character/lore control, not a proven fidelity winner. |
| Character Card V3 — MIT [G03] | Portable character format; not a model or memory system. | Client implementation/version support varies. | Export only if a chosen client uses it. Keep this Markdown as the canonical source. |
| Letta Code — Apache-2.0 [G04] | Stateful agent harness with editable memory blocks, git-tracked context, channels, local/cloud options, Windows x64 support. | Active implementation differs from retired V1 tutorials; automatic reflection can mutate state. | Optional for deliberate inspectable cross-session state; protect the approved core from automatic rewrites. |
| Mem0 — Apache-2.0 [G05] | Memory library/service integrated by a developer into retrieve → prompt → answer → save. | Requires a surrounding app, inference/embedding/storage decisions, and permissions. | Use within a selected custom application when a measured memory need justifies integration. No native persona bridge established. |
| Graphiti — Apache-2.0 [G06] | Temporal context graph with fact history/provenance. | Database, model/embedder, ingestion, authentication, and operations. | Defer unless changing-fact provenance defeats a simpler ledger. |
| Open WebUI — custom Open WebUI license [G07] | Self-hosted multi-model browser/PWA chat, instructions, memory, voice. | Hosting/local hardware or APIs; current branding terms and exceptions differ from plain MIT/BSD. | Optional local/private model interface; alternative to LibreChat. |
| LibreChat — MIT [G08] | Multi-provider web agents/presets, explicit user/agent memory, STT/TTS. | Several services in common deployment; provider/voice/hosting costs. | Optional API/multiuser interface if those features justify burden. |
| promptfoo — MIT [G09] | File-based prompt/evaluation runner and reports. | Configured providers and LLM graders can incur cost and receive data; optional cloud and telemetry are separate. | Preferred optional evaluator when repeated comparisons justify automation. |
| OpenAI Evals source — MIT code, dataset exceptions [G10] | Python framework/benchmark registry. | More setup and evaluation calls; data licenses vary. | Research resource; unnecessary for minimum native installation. Hosted Evals retirement is a different product. |
| OpenAI Codex — Apache-2.0 [G11] | Existing worker with documented instruction/configuration mechanisms. | Plan/provider limits and actual tool permissions remain. | Keep; do not replace merely to obtain a persona. |
| OpenAI Realtime Agents demo — MIT [G12] | Custom voice-app development example with tools/handoffs. | Demo, not finished companion; own hosting, authentication, API cost, mobile/audio testing. | Optional only for a concrete voice requirement beyond native products. Verify current API before adapting old example names. |
| Goose — aaif-goose/goose; Apache-2.0 [G13] | General local agent with provider/MCP choices and Windows support. | Overlaps Codex/Cindy execution role. | Defer; no demonstrated incremental persona value here. |
| Ollama — MIT engine [G14] | Local/cloud inference runtime; model licenses are separate. | Owned hardware, memory, latency, energy, updates; Android requires a client/host arrangement. | Optional only for an explicit local inference need. |

### 12.2 Cindy-specific findings

The supplied repository is relevant, not a discarded placeholder. Its README identifies the open client and a separate backend. Current source describes official service sign-in, supported plan authorization, API keys, and local models; Skip Sign-In loses server-backed features. Do not describe it as a completely self-hosted full backend or unlimited free inference [G01].

Release v0.1.114 (2026-10-22) reports continuous companion calls, pause-to-send, sentence-wise response reading, interruption, and companion voice/speed preferences. v0.1.115 (2026-10-23) adds Qwen/CosyVoice-related support. Those are shipped-feature claims, not measurements of this user's Russian, latency, interrupt control, or persona consistency [G01a], [G01b].

The mobile architecture document describes a device-link controller. Test PC awake/offline, reconnect, Android foreground/background, interrupted calls, and which machine actually executes. A phone app does not imply autonomous execution with the PC asleep [G01c].

Official-build analytics are described by the author as device/OS/app metadata rather than chat/file content. That statement is not an independent traffic audit and does not mean remote model/service calls keep all data on the device. Inspect actual data paths and permissions for a trial [G01].

Cindy's young project history and rapidly shipped voice features make a bounded sandbox trial preferable to a wholesale migration. Preserve native ChatGPT and the existing assistant. Do not migrate private persona archives or account credentials merely to audition a voice.

### 12.3 Important format/runtime distinctions

In SillyTavern, a character card describes the assistant; a persona describes the user's identity. Put Lucifer in the character configuration. Speech integrations can map voices to characters, but they do not reproduce native ChatGPT realtime behavior automatically [G02a], [G02b].

The active Letta implementation is letta-ai/letta-code; older server tutorials may target its retired V1. Cloud is the default and stores identity, memory and conversations. Bundled default prompts can become Cloud-managed on resume; custom prompts remain explicit. For a deliberately selected Cloud deployment, the documented LETTA_CODE_PRESERVE_CLOUD_SYSTEM_PROMPT=1 option may prevent automatic default-prompt updates. AgentFile .af import/export was removed. Native Windows automatic client reflection defaults off, while manual reflection remains; WSL/server behavior differs. Inspect actual existing state before migration [G04].

The private MGrinch/future-memory repository was found as an existing research/blueprint lead. Its README did not establish a native Android Voice bridge or automatic native ChatGPT retrieval. A historical local Letta claim is not a current service check. Reuse proven existing work if available; do not build a second system based only on the project's name.

Open WebUI memory is not merely its knowledge-base RAG; LibreChat also has explicit user/agent memory. Neither is automatically ChatGPT account memory. Local-model configurations need not incur per-token API fees, but require compute and maintenance. A ChatGPT subscription is not a general OpenAI API allowance [G05], [G06], [G07], [G08], [G09].

### 12.4 Selection by observed deficit

| Observed unmet goal after native baseline | One candidate | Minimum proof before adoption |
|---|---|---|
| Need a phone-accessible agent executing on the PC while conversing | Cindy | One real end-to-end task, accepted voice, reconnect/interrupt behavior, understood access/cost. |
| Need portable character lore and direct prompt/card control | SillyTavern | Export/import fidelity, fresh-session behavior, practical Android access, tolerable voice path. |
| Need inspectable durable state across a custom agent's channels | Letta Code | Correct write/read/update/delete with provenance; core not silently changed. |
| Existing custom app needs selective factual memory | Mem0 | Better actual recall/update behavior than a simple ledger, with correct isolation. |
| Need fact-validity intervals and conflicting historical facts | Graphiti | Concrete cases simpler memory fails, acceptable operating burden. |
| Need local model data control | Open WebUI + an appropriate runtime, or an already installed equivalent | Actual hardware latency/quality/voice testing and model-license review. |
| Need API-centric multi-provider/multiuser interface | LibreChat | Required agent and speech behavior works; service maintenance accepted. |
| Need custom realtime turn-taking or voice orchestration | Current official Live/Realtime API route + suitable demo | Required behavior on desktop/mobile, credentials protected, bounded usage cost. |
| Prompt comparisons are becoming repetitive | promptfoo | Valid prompts include every test input/history; saved reports reduce repeated manual work. |

### 12.5 Optional repository installation procedure

Do not execute this branch just to make the solution look complete. Enter it only for an observed gap and an authorized choice of runtime. For the chosen repository:

1. Resolve the canonical owner/repository; read current README, license, releases, installation instructions, security notes, and dependencies at an inspected revision.
2. Record the chosen release/commit and why. A researched head commit is a provenance reference, not an assertion that it is the safest release to install.
3. Inspect the actual PC for an existing installation, runtime, models, service ports, and unrelated work. Prefer reusing a working setup.
4. Use a contained test directory and non-sensitive demonstration data. Do not execute downloaded shell/PowerShell pipes automatically because a README prints them. Inspect any installation script and follow the host's approval policy.
5. For a source checkout, clone only the selected repository into the chosen work directory and verify the checked-out commit. GitHub is the source location; do not upload Misha's private corpus to it without explicit publication scope.
6. Follow that release's documented platform commands. Do not invent one universal pnpm/Docker/npm command for every project. Record actual versions and errors.
7. Configure only the minimum model/voice/backend needed. Credential entry uses the supported secret/auth path, not logged command arguments, screenshots of tokens, or committed files.
8. Put the canonical character into the actual instruction/card field; map only appropriate memory into the chosen state store. Preserve fictional tags and supersession.
9. Run the same relevant scenarios used in native baseline, plus platform-specific lifecycle tests. Compare actual observations, maintenance, and cost.
10. Keep or remove the isolated trial according to evidence and the user's goal. Do not replace native apps, create startup services, or schedule automatic reflection by default. A required loopback listener is part of a selected local web app; new LAN/public exposure needs an actual connectivity requirement within the authorized deployment. Configure only the authenticated access needed for a chosen phone-access setup.

For local Windows Codex already present, no reinstall is needed for this persona. If actually absent and installation is authorized, use current official Windows instructions [G11/O23]; the documented npm package is @openai/codex. Verify the installed version and effective model/effort. Do not copy a macOS/Linux shell installer into Windows or call a launch command an installer.
